title: DexCare Acquires Mila Health, Extending AI Agents From Scheduling to Care Coordination
key_facts: DexCare announced the acquisition of Mila Health, an AI care coordination company whose agents call, text and chat with patients to get them scheduled, prepared and seen.
Mila runs on DexCare's access data model, which DexCare says is proven across more than 10 million bookings.
Mila says its agents achieve a 54% patient response rate in outbound outreach, 80% higher than manual call centers, and reduce no-show rates by 50% and increase revenue by 18%.
Tampa General Hospital's Dr. Peter Chang says DexCare codified 260 scheduling policies and uncovered more than 50 gaps.
DexCare spun out of Providence Health in 2021 and has raised $146 million to date, including a $75 million Series C round led by ICONIQ Growth in 2023.
The article gives no purchase price or deal terms.
Mila is described as API-first, able to launch AI agents in hours.
quote_evidence: DexCare, Inc. today announced the acquisition of Mila Health (Mila), an AI care coordination company whose agents call, text, and chat with patients to get them scheduled, prepared, and seen.
In production, its agents achieve a 54% patient response rate during outbound outreach, which is 80% higher than manual call centers.
Mila agents reduce no-show rates by 50% and increase revenue by 18%.
why_it_matters_hint: A patient-scheduling company is adding AI agents that contact patients directly, though the performance figures are company claims.
notes: The article is a company press release run by Healthcare IT Today; all figures are company claims and no price is given.
